title: The Double Deadline Anew
premise: Rosalind Marchetti, a disgraced intelligence analyst fired from three agencies, has spent five years as a low-level compliance contractor, following protocols that shift without warning. When Flight 4472 vanishes from every database while still airborne—and lands carrying one passenger too many—Ros traces the anomaly to the Consortium, the black-budget training network that shaped him and erased his own file. To survive, he must weaponize the tradecraft they burned into him against them, racing a double deadline: the Consortium's purge of all 'legacy assets' in fourteen days, and the landing of a second ghost flight carrying something far worse. In the end Ros burns the network's central archive at the cost of his own last records of who he was before, choosing an unwritten future over a curated past.
about_author: I. M. Kavanagh is the pen name of a former aviation logistics consultant who spent a decade inside the paperwork of companies that officially never existed. The Double Deadline Anew is their third thriller and first written entirely from memory.

chapters.title: Compliance
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind Marchetti. Five years after his third firing, Ros audits shipping manifests for a firm that doesn't technically exist, obeying rulebooks that change overnight. A routine flag on Flight 4472 should be nothing. The emotional beat is numb competence—the quiet dread of a man who has learned that noticing things is what gets you fired.

chapters.title: One Passenger Too Many
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Cross-referencing gate footage with the manifest, he counts twenty-nine bodies boarding, thirty deplaning. He files the discrepancy through proper channels; within an hour the flight itself ceases to exist mid-air. Beat: cold vertigo—the rules just rewrote reality, not the other way around.

chapters.title: The Rewritten Rulebook
chapters.summary: POV Ros. His access revokes itself retroactively; yesterday's emails now show he never sent them. He recognizes the signature style of the erasure—it matches how his own personnel file was scrubbed five years ago. Beat: recognition curdling into terror. Someone is using the same machine on him.

chapters.title: What They Trained Me For
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter, POV Ros. Memory fragments surface: a facility called Meridian House, instructors who taught him to build and unbuild identities. He realizes the Consortium didn't fire him—they released a prototype into the wild to see if it would degrade. Beat: grief for the self he can't fully remember.

chapters.title: The Dead Drop That Isn't
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Following tradecraft he never consciously learned, he finds a dead drop he apparently established years ago and forgot. Inside: a burner phone already ringing. A voice tells him he has fourteen days before 'legacy assets' are purged. Beat: the trap was also a lifeline.

chapters.title: Dana Okafor
chapters.summary: POV Dana Okafor, a former Meridian instructor turned archivist, living under her third name. She receives Ros's signal and must decide whether to answer it or report it. Beat: divided loyalty—she helped erase him once and has regretted it ever since.

chapters.title: Fourteen Days
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Meeting Dana in a rail station, he learns the purge schedule: every asset trained at Meridian House will be retired when the archive migrates to a new server farm. The second ghost flight, he learns, carries the migration's key custodian. Beat: the deadline acquires a face and a body count.

chapters.title: Ghost Flight Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Dana. She explains how flights are vanished—not hacked but administratively unborn, deleted across forty systems by people with legitimate keys. Ros understands the horror: no conspiracy, just procedure. Beat: institutional evil rendered banal, and more frightening for it.

chapters.title: The Man Who Boarded Twice
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Tracking the extra passenger—a man named Elias Voss—he finds Voss boarded two flights in two cities at the same hour. One of them is still walking around. Beat: uncanny pursuit; Ros realizes he's chasing someone built by the same hands.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement, Revised
chapters.summary: POV Ros. The Consortium makes contact through his landlord, offering reinstatement if he delivers Dana. The offer is generous, warm, almost paternal. Beat: temptation—five years of precarity versus belonging, and he hates how much he wants to say yes.

chapters.title: Meridian House, Remembered
chapters.summary: POV Dana, interwoven with Ros's recovered memories. The training wasn't interrogation; it was curation—children taught that memory is a liability and obedience a form of love. Beat: shared trauma becoming fragile trust between two survivors.

chapters.title: The Custodian
chapters.summary: POV Ros. He identifies the migration's key custodian: Dr. Imre Halasz, the architect of Meridian's curriculum, flying incognito on the next ghost flight. Killing or saving Halasz decides everything. Beat: moral vertigo—the monster is also the only person who might restore Ros's erased memories.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, Three Funerals
chapters.summary: POV Ros. He revisits the handlers who fired him and finds two dead in 'accidents' and one willing to talk—for immunity. She confirms the Consortium sits inside the agencies themselves, not beside them. Beat: betrayal at scale; there is no outside to run to.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Hiding Ros in her safehouse, she calculates odds like an actuary: survival requires either the archive destroyed or the purge list stolen. Both require Halasz alive long enough to unlock things. Beat: reluctant partnership hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Ghost flight two is scheduled; its manifest lists Halasz under a name Ros recognizes as his own childhood surname. The Consortium is baiting him personally. Beat: fury and flattery entwined—he was never invisible, only inventory.

chapters.title: Elias Voss, Found
chapters.summary: POV Ros. He corners Voss, the doubled passenger, in a freight yard. Voss claims to be another legacy asset running his own countdown, and offers proof: a partial copy of the purge list. Beat: uneasy alliance with a mirror—who may be exactly what he seems, which is worse.

chapters.title: The List Has Your Name On It
chapters.summary: POV Dana. The partial list confirms it: 214 names, Ros near the top, Dana beneath him. But the list also contains names of people already dead for years—the purge happened once before, quietly. Beat: historical horror; this is recurrence, not innovation.

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Captured briefly by a Consortium retrieval team, he endures not torture but a review—a performance evaluation conducted mid-abduction, scoring his loyalty metrics aloud. Beat: psychological violation; the institution's cruelest weapon is treating people as data.

chapters.title: Extraction, Improvised
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Using Meridian extraction protocols against Meridian's own team, Dana pulls Ros out, burning a decade of careful anonymity. Beat: cost made concrete—she is now on the list in practice as well as paper.

chapters.title: Halfway Mark
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Seven days left. Wounded, exhausted, he and Dana take stock: they have a partial list, a target (Halasz), and a plan forming around the archive migration itself. Beat: grim midpoint resolve—the hunted begin designing the hunt.

chapters.title: The Server Farm at Keflavík
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Recon of the Icelandic facility where the archive will live: biometric locks keyed to Halasz, air-gapped, guarded by contractors who believe they protect weather data. Beat: the plan crystallizes—get in during migration, when the doors open widest.

chapters.title: Voss's Double Game
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Voss's copy of the list proves subtly doctored; he's feeding them a version designed to steer their approach into a kill zone. Confronting him, Ros can't tell if Voss is traitor, triple agent, or genuinely terrified. Beat: paranoia as atmosphere—trust becomes a tactical resource.

chapters.title: What Halasz Built
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Researching Halasz's early career, she finds his original academic work on 'adaptive memory suppression'—and a photograph of the first cohort of children. Ros is in it. So is she. Beat: devastating intimacy; their whole relationship was designed before they met.

chapters.title: The Offer He Can't Refuse
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Halasz contacts Ros directly: surrender Dana, and Ros gets his full file back—every erased year, every manufactured memory identified. Beat: the book's cruelest fork—truth about himself versus loyalty to the only person who chose him freely.

chapters.title: Dana's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Knowing Ros's temptation, Dana preempts it: she gives him her own Meridian file, unredacted, including the orders she followed to erase him. Beat: radical honesty as gambit—if trust survives this, it's real; if not, better to know now.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: POV Ros. He refuses Halasz. The refusal triggers contingency: the purge accelerates, and assets worldwide start dying ahead of schedule. Beat: consequences cascade—principles have a body count, and Ros starts keeping score.

chapters.title: Running the Kill Zone Anyway
chapters.summary: POV Ros and Dana alternating. They use Voss's poisoned route deliberately, feeding false telemetry so the ambushers ambush each other. Beat: turning the enemy's certainty into a weapon—the analysts' revenge.

chapters.title: Voss, Redeemed or Not
chapters.summary: POV Voss, first time. His interiority reveals a man who sabotaged the list hoping either side's victory would end his own countdown. He dies covering their escape, passing Ros a genuine key fragment. Beat: tragic ambiguity resolved too late to matter.

chapters.title: Six Days: The Ascent Plan
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Final plan set: enter Keflavík during migration window, force Halasz to unlock the archive, copy the true purge list to expose the Consortium publicly, then burn the servers. Beat: hope with a fuse attached.

chapters.title: In Through the Weather Door
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Infiltration begins under cover of a supply convoy; Ros poses as a contractor using credentials Voss died to deliver. Beat: taut suspense—the old training working perfectly, which frightens him more than failure would.

chapters.title: Halasz, Face to Face
chapters.summary: POV Ros. He reaches Halasz in the migration control room. The old man isn't afraid; he's proud, greeting Ros like a finished thesis. Beat: confrontation as family drama—the creator meeting the creation that came back.

chapters.title: The Archive Opens
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Under duress, Halasz unlocks the archive. Dana copies the true list while Ros searches his own file—and finds the entry blank except for one word: 'RESERVED.' Beat: revelation withheld; even here, his identity is someone else's property.

chapters.title: Reserved For What
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Halasz, savoring leverage, explains: Ros was never a failed asset but the reserve custodian—the intended inheritor of the whole network. The firings were curriculum. Beat: the blurb's promise detonates—staying invisible was never an option because he was the succession plan.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Refused
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Offered the network—power, permanence, his own history restored—Ros declines, and the refusal breaks something in Halasz more than any bullet could. Beat: thematic climax; corruption dies not by exposure alone but by an heir who won't sign.

chapters.title: Burn It All
chapters.summary: POV Dana and Ros. With the list exfiltrated via satellite uplink to forty newsrooms, they trigger the thermite protocol. Halasz stays with his archive. Beat: cathartic destruction—the library of curated selves going up in white fire.

chapters.title: Extraction Under Fire
chapters.summary: POV Ros. The facility's guards, learning what they guarded, turn chaotic; Ros and Dana fight out through collapsing corridors, Ros dragging a wounded stranger because some rules deserve keeping. Beat: action climax fused with character proof.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Dana. The purge list goes public; arrests ripple through three agencies. But the Consortium was procedural, not personal—somewhere, successors are reading the post-mortem. Beat: victory with a shadow; systems outlive their architects.

chapters.title: The File That Stays Blank
chapters.summary: POV Ros. Offered reconstructed records by investigators, Ros declines. Whatever he was before belongs to the people who wrote it. Beat: quiet resolution of the memory theme—an identity chosen beats an identity issued.

chapters.title: Two Names, No Handlers
chapters.summary: POV Ros and Dana. Weeks later, in a coastal town under names that are merely theirs, they rebuild ordinary life badly and gladly. A letter arrives containing a single word: 'RESERVED.' Beat: peace shadowed by inheritance—the past keeps mailing forwarding addresses.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: POV Ros. He burns the letter unread, then writes a new rulebook—one page, one rule: notice things anyway. Final beat: the analyst who was trained to obey chooses to remain awake, and the double deadline dissolves into a single open-ended day.
